But I still see this removed in the latest patchset..

@gunnar@gmills.xyz
The objPath.filename() == chassisId check is required in
handleChassisGetSubTree to ensure only the requested chassis is returned,
since the mapper subtree can contain multiple inventory objects.

In handleChassisPatch, the check is not required because the PATCH flow is
already scoped to the requested chassis and exits after the first applicable
match. The behavior was verified to work correctly without this check.

(e.g. EBADR / InvalidArgs) to be translated to Redfish errors.

Thank you for the review and suggestions.

The code has been updated to remove redundant comments, use `auto` for DBus
container types to improve readability and consistency with existing code,
retain the `chassisId` filtering logic, and simplify the implementation by
relying on DBus error handling rather than explicit interface pre-checks.

Please clarify this.   The CHASSIS AssetTag is read only.  The ComputerSystem AssetTag has been settable for a long time.

Thanks for pointing this out. This change specifically targets the Chassis AssetTag, which was previously read-only. While the ComputerSystem AssetTag has been writable for some time, this patch enables write support for the Chassis AssetTag and ensures the updated value is propagated to the backing FRU via Entity Manager.
I'm not sure how this could work as designed.  You need to set the AssetTag on the backing device.  This will set the EM flag.

This is handled by the backend Entity Manager change (Change-Id: I1c921d7e68f6c9ad1ae75a0e00f74b0164150ad1).

PR: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/entity-manager/+/86091

When AssetTag is updated via Redfish or set-property, Entity Manager propagates the value to the corresponding FRU interface (backing device). This ensures the EM flag is set correctly and the value persists across BMC reboots.
